item.title: Jean 0.4.15
item.description:
Jean 0.4.15

Everything planned for 0.4.14, which was pulled within the hour: its hub was missing, so the hub and your tabs showed blank pages. 0.4.15 is the same release with a complete hub.

Releases never ship without the hub

- The hub is built once more if its build fails, and a release stops when the hub is incomplete. - `jean install` refuses an app without a built hub instead of rebuilding inside it (that rebuild is what emptied the hub on 3 Nov).

"Waiting on you" updates again

- The pinned list stopped updating once it got long (Slack said the message was too long, though Jean had kept it under Slack's limit). Slack counts each emoji by its name (✅ is `:white_check_mark:`) and some characters twice; Jean now counts the same way. If Slack still refuses an edit, Jean sends a list half as long instead of none, with "…and N more" pointing to Today on the hub.

Jean always runs from Applications

- After a release, opening "Jean" could start the freshly built copy in the build folder instead of the one in Applications, and that copy took over Jean's background services (Slack bridge, hub, nightly jobs). The next build would have replaced it under them. Now: - The app only takes over the background services from Applications. A copy anywhere else shows a note and leaves the team as it is. - `jean install` refuses to run from a build folder (`JEAN_INSTALL_ANYWHERE=1` overrides). - Releasing leaves the built app zipped, so macOS can't open it by name. - `jean install` repoints the Slack bridge's Python when the app has moved, so the bridge doesn't stop at its next restart.

Helpers start (and stop) again

- Claude Code 2.1 reports a new background session with a short id only. Jean read that as "failed to start", so helpers for a busy specialist ran and finished but were never tracked or stopped. Jean now takes the full id from Claude's own record of that session, only when its name and folder match the helper.

Fewer asks, fewer posts

- **Merge on your ✅ alone (opt-in).** With `github.adminMergeAfterSlack` turned on, a ✅'d merge ask lets the lane merge that pull request itself with GitHub's admin bypass, once, within the ask's two hours; merge asks stop saying "Approve on GitHub" and Waiting on you stops listing "no GitHub Approve yet". Off by default. - **One ask for a plan across lanes.** A job several specialists do in turn (put the content worker live, import and post, put it back) is one ask: the owner sees the steps as a numbered list, and one ✅ lets each specialist do its own steps. - **Approvals no longer post "Approved by …".** The ask itself now shows who approved it, what it allows and until when. - **Jean checks before asking you to tick.** `jean ask --list --task <id>` shows a task's asks and their state; the manual tells Jean to check it first, and to check a content tool's test mode before asking to publish.

Quieter Slack, conversations that stay together

- Your messages go straight to Jean, ahead of the specialists' own messages to each other. "X is restarting" now appears only when a delivery really failed for 45 seconds, once per thread, and changes to "Passed on to X." when it's delivered. - Every file Jean posts carries a line saying what it is: no more empty file messages. Several files can go in one post. - One "Files from the request, copied to…" line per task, naming every specialist that got them. - No extra "Waiting on the person" pointer when the specialist already said it waits on you. - A follow-up in an active conversation is never moved to a new thread. Only a new request after a quiet spell, in a thread holding 8 tasks or more, gets its own thread. - Team members allowed to ask directly (`claude.directMembers`) are named in the manual, so Jean takes their requests instead of answering "owners only".

Keys and the Mac, from your phone

- **Team keys:** Settings › Keys › Add key stores a named key (say STRIPE_TEST_SECRET_KEY). A specialist asks for one with `jean keys request`, which posts where to add it, once. A specialist uses it with `jean keys run <NAME> -- <command>`, after your ✅ on that exact command: the key is never shown to it, and printed output is masked. - `jean disk` shows free space and what takes it, without sudo; folders it can't read are named instead. - Specialists never ask you to type in Terminal or use sudo.

The nightly review

- Every night after the 04:00 restart, `jean review` counts the day from 7 AM: your messages and Jean's, chases, corrections, asks, noise, thread moves, outages. It compares with the week before and saves a report in the Library (project "Jean ops"). Ops then posts the trends and up to three suggested changes in #jean-ops. Nothing changes without your ✅. `jean review --dry` shows it any time. - Settings: `review.enabled`, `review.lane` (ops), `review.dayStart` ("07:00").

item.title: Jean 0.4.13
item.description:
Jean 0.4.13

Fewer, clearer approvals, and a task thread that's easier to follow.

  • **One approval for a job of several steps.** A job that needs the same kind of action a few times (a carousel import's start, upload and finish, say) now asks you once. The post says "covers 3 steps", and your one ✅ lets the specialist do those steps within the usual two hours. Up to 10 steps; anything else still asks for each action.
  • **Asks can be withdrawn.** When you change the plan (another artist, a dropped job), the team takes back the asks that no longer apply. The post then reads "Withdrawn: …" with no buttons, it leaves Waiting on you, and pressing Approve on it does nothing. Before, stale asks just sat there with live buttons until they ran out.
  • **Jean checks what's already made.** Before starting something new, Jean looks in the Library for a match and says what's already there, with a link. No more "waiting on Growth" for a set that already exists.
  • **The task card follows the conversation.** When you reply in a task's thread, its card moves down to just below your message, so you see the progress where you're reading. There's still only one card, and its Approve button still works after it moves.
  • **One ask per job, with the right kind.** When the guard stops an action, it now names the exact kind of approval it needs and suggests one ask for the whole job. A second ask for the same task within a few minutes is marked "(2nd ask for this task)", and Jean is told so it can combine or withdraw them.
  • **No more waiting for ever on a tap Jean can't see.** If a task has waited on you for 15 minutes, Jean checks whether you already did it some other way (in a product's own console, or on GitHub) and finishes the task if you did. Owners can change the 15 minutes with `slack.waitRecheckMinutes` (0 turns it off).

item.title: Jean 0.4.12
item.description:
Jean 0.4.12

A fix for 0.4.11's "Waiting on you" message.

  • **The list keeps updating.** When the list grew past 4,000 characters, Slack refused every edit, so the message stopped changing after it was first posted. Now it shows as many lines as fit and ends with "…and N more", linking to the Today page on the hub.
  • **The pin takes after you reinstall the Slack app.** If the message was posted before the app had the `pins:write` permission, Jean now pins it on a later update, within about 10 minutes. Before, it never tried again.

item.title: Jean 0.4.11
item.description:
Jean 0.4.11

Slack that's easier to follow: one pinned list of what's waiting on you, one thread per topic with a clear title, the latest version of every deliverable one tap away, and fewer things that slowed the team down.

Before you start: one change in your Slack app

Jean now pins its "Waiting on you" message, which needs one more permission:

1. Open api.slack.com/apps › Jean. 2. **OAuth & Permissions › Bot Token Scopes:** add `pins:write`. 3. Press **Reinstall to Workspace** and allow.

Without it, the message is still posted and kept up to date, just not pinned.

After installing, restart the Slack bridge once: `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.jean.bridge`.

Slack: what's waiting on you

- One **Waiting on you** message in the main channel, pinned and edited in place (never reposted). One line each, with a link: approvals waiting for your ✅, PRs that still need your **Approve** or **Merge** on GitHub, and board cards waiting on you. - Merge asks now start with **Approve on GitHub**, because a merge needs both your ✅ in Slack and GitHub's Approve. The PR stays on the list until it's merged. - The hub has a **Today** page with the same list.

Slack: one thread per topic

- The separate "X is on it" message is gone. The task card shows which specialist has it, with a link to their work thread. One task, one card, one answer. - When a thread already holds 5 tasks, Jean moves the next new request to its own thread. A new topic in a thread gets moved too. - Tasks are tagged with a project, and thread titles read like "[Jeorgia pitch] reviewer fixes". `jean projects` lists the projects. - The routing message no longer shows a raw link like `<https://…|in #jean-growth>`. (#110)

Finding the latest file

- Each project's deliverable has one Library entry marked **Latest**, with older versions folded underneath it. One link always opens the newest version, and final answers link to it instead of attaching a new file every round. - A new **Projects** page on the hub shows, for each project, its status, its latest files, and what's waiting on whom.

Files

- Files you attach to a request are copied into the specialist's own folder when the task goes to them, so nobody has to copy them by hand. - Specialists can attach text files (emails, changelogs, logs: .md, .txt, .eml and more) instead of squeezing long text into a reply. Text files you attach in Slack come through too. - `jean slack post` gives back where the message went, so replies and files can go under it. `jean slack new-thread "<title>"` starts a titled thread.

Reliability

- A message for a specialist who is restarting waits and is passed on once they're back, in order, instead of "send this again". Messages they were sent just before a restart are sent again to the new session. - Specialists message each other with `jean tell <specialist> "<message>"`, which waits the same way, instead of a direct message that a restart could lose. Specialists are addressed by their own name, never by an old session label like "Build [f168eb]". - Specialists work in their own folder again. Claude Code had started moving each one into a separate worktree copy before its first edit, and from there it couldn't commit in its own checkout (Build and #231). Jean now turns that off for its specialists (`claude.bgIsolation` in Jean's settings file changes it); helpers and workers still get their own worktrees from Jean. - Board card ids carry the specialist's name, so one specialist can't overwrite another's card by reusing an id.

Team

- An owner can let named team members ask Jean directly, without a ✅ for each request: `claude.directMembers` in Jean's settings file. They still can't approve anything. Off by default. On a personal Claude plan (Free, Pro, Max) this is the owner's own choice and account: Anthropic's terms keep those plans to one person.

Security and fewer false stops (the guard)

- Jean can start a helper for a busy specialist (`jean overflow ask`), as the manual says. Before, the guard stopped it, and work sat waiting. - A script that only reads files in a `.claude` folder (another specialist's worktree, say) is no longer stopped as "starting a Claude session". Starting Claude from a script still asks. - Adding a project is Jean's job; every specialist can read the list. - `jean tell --file` never reads a secret, and code can't use Jean's message queue to pass a note off as one from Slack.

item.title: Jean 0.4.10
item.description:
Jean 0.4.10

One Slack channel per specialist, a clearer Task details window, and a round of guard fixes. Install it soon: the guard fixes close gaps a lane could use to act without asking.

Before you start: one change in your Slack app

Jean can now link a channel when you invite it. For that, the Slack app needs one more event and two more permissions:

1. Open api.slack.com/apps › Jean. 2. **Event Subscriptions › Subscribe to bot events:** add `member_joined_channel`. 3. **OAuth & Permissions › Bot Token Scopes:** add `channels:read` and `groups:read`. 4. Press **Reinstall to Workspace** and allow.

Without this, everything else works. Inviting Jean just doesn't link a channel, and you can still link one by hand (below).

After installing, restart the Slack bridge once so it picks up the new Slack features: `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.jean.bridge`.

Slack: a channel for each specialist

- #jean stays the main channel: requests, approvals, answers and daily briefs. Each specialist can also have its own channel, like #jean-build or #jean-research. (#94) - When a task goes to a specialist with its own channel, a thread opens there with that specialist's steps, linked from your request. The answer still comes back in your thread. (#94) - To give a specialist a channel, an owner creates `#jean-<specialist>` (for example `#jean-research`) and invites @Jean. Jean links it and says hello. An invite from a team member, or to a channel with another name, links nothing. (#98) - You can also link one by hand on the Mac: `jean slack channels link research <channel id>`. `jean slack channels` lists them. (#94) - A request posted straight into a specialist's channel is that specialist's task, answered there. (#94) - If you unlink a channel, open tasks stop posting there. (#96)

Slack: a clearer Task details window

- **Details** on a task now starts with a plain summary: who asked, what they asked, and what was done or is happening now. (#95) - Below that are two short sections, each with **More**. **Simple** says who worked on it and what the last step was. **Technical**, for owners only, says what was touched (counts of commands and edits, files, estimated cost) without pasting commands. (#95) - "Asked by" shows the person who asked, not Jean. (#95)

Security (the guard)

- **Stricter, as you chose:** writing to a file whose name the guard can't see (a variable set in an earlier step, or names read from a list) now asks. Names it can work out, temporary folders and your home folder pass. (#103, ask a5f370e) - **Stricter, as you chose:** curl that sends a change to an address the guard can't see now asks, whatever the site. (#102, ask a240fec) - Changes to GitHub made from code (Python's requests, Node's fetch and others) are judged like `gh` and curl. Changes to organisation settings, SSH keys and email addresses ask too. curl pointed at another settings file (`CURL_HOME`) asks. (#102) - A command split over two lines with `\` is now judged as one, so a delete or a push to main can't slip past by being split. (#101) - Recursive deletes from code outside the lane's folder ask, however the code reaches them, including paths that climb out with `..`. Plain `rm -rf` now catches those too. (#106) - git options that could hide a push to main, or run a command from a setting, are read correctly. So is `gh workflow run --ref main deploy.yml`. (#105) - Linking or unlinking a specialist's Slack channel is an owner's job. (#104)

Fewer false stops

- A script line continued with `\` is read as one line, so Research's PDF renderer runs again. (#101)

Reliability

- The Slack bridge and `jean slack channels` no longer overwrite each other's settings changes. (#98) - If the settings file stays busy, Jean gives up after 10 seconds instead of hanging. Your request or ✅ still goes through; an invite or a pairing message gets "try again in a moment". (#100) - `jean progress --summary` on a stopped task now tells the lane it was stopped. (#97)

item.title: Jean 0.4.9
item.description:
Jean 0.4.9

A security update for the guard, plus fewer false stops. Install it soon.

Security (the guard)

- Merging, publishing a release, deleting or archiving a repo, or starting a deploy through GitHub's API now asks for your ✅, just as gh's own commands do. That covers `gh api`, curl, wget and httpie. Any other change to a repo through the API asks too, unless it's everyday work like comments, issues, pull requests, labels or rerunning CI. (#93) - A lane can't mark its own CI as passed, move a branch, or commit a file through GitHub's API without asking. (#93) - `gh auth token` and `gh auth status --show-token` no longer print your GitHub token to a lane. (#81) - Recursive deletes from inside a script (Python and others) outside the lane's folder ask, like `rm -rf`. (#87) - curl's and wget's settings files (`~/.curlrc`, `~/.wgetrc`) are protected like `~/.netrc`. (#93)

Fewer false stops

- gh commands that only read from GitHub pass in the developer's Jean checkout. `gh pr checkout` and `gh repo sync` there still stop. (#81) - sed ranges built with shell arithmetic, like `$((s+45))`, pass. (#82) - `cd -` goes back to the folder before, so the guard knows where the next command runs. (#90) - `jean levels` with a word it doesn't know says how to list the levels. (#91)

Slack

- When buttons are off, a task card's ask moves to its own post instead of waiting on the card. (#88) - Tell me never shows a lane's slug, and a failed save doesn't post the same events twice. (#89)

item.title: Jean 0.4.8
item.description:
Jean 0.4.8

A security update for the guard. Install it soon.

Security (the guard)

- A merge, release or deploy through `gh` asks for your ✅ again, however the command is written. Some ways of writing gh's options could get past that check. Merges through GitHub's API (GraphQL included) are covered too. (#83) - A lane can't change Jean's files, its approval records included, through some ways of writing a `sed` command. The guard now reads sed scripts the way sed does, scripts in a file too, and every way of asking sed to edit a file in place. (#84, #86) - A sed script that runs a command still asks when it only reads one of Jean's files. (#86) - A lane can't write into Jean's folders through a line whose folder changes the guard can't follow (popd, a `cd` in brackets or a pipe, a `cd` that fails): such a line is checked in every folder it reached. (#92) - `git fetch` and `git remote update` in the developer's Jean checkout now stop like other changes there: they write into it. In a lane's own repo they still pass. (#80)

item.title: Jean 0.4.7
item.description:
Jean 0.4.7

Changes since 0.4.6 (d03b84c), merged into slack-tidy (39f9e23), #69–#79.

New

- Approval levels: for each lane, owners choose how much it may do without a ✅. Merges, deploys, publishing, spending, sending outside the team and deleting can each be **Ask** (as before), **Tell me** (goes ahead; Jean posts what it did in Slack) or **Allow** (goes ahead; listed in the day's digest after 18:00). Set them in Settings › Approvals or with `jean levels`; lanes can see theirs but not change them. (#70) - Trust windows: a lane, or Jean for any lane, can ask in Slack for up to 8 hours of Tell me. One ✅ turns it on. (#70) - Whatever the levels, these still ask: starting Claude sessions, background jobs, hooks, anything touching Jean's own files, the coordinator, each connection's tools (they follow the connection's own setting), and deletes outside a lane's own work. (#70, #72) - Slack task card: each step gets its own row with the tool's icon (GitHub, Stripe, PostHog…), a live line says what kind of step is running ("running a command", "editing a file"), and the done card lists the tools used. (#73, #78) - Details on the card: the step log for everyone; for owners also a peek at the last moves, the files changed and the cost so far. Secrets are hidden in the peek. (#73, #76) - Approving in the card: a lane's ask about a merge, deploy, publish, payment, message or delete shows on the task's card with Approve / Not yet. On a card only the button approves; a ✅ reaction there does nothing. Other asks keep their own post. (#74, #75) - Tell me posts and the evening digest look like the card. In the channel they say only which lane did what kind of action and when; See the list (owners only) shows what each one ran. (#75, #76, #79) - Slack: the "On it" card shows Jean's animated step marks: a silver comet while a step runs, a green tick when it's done, a desk bell while a task waits on you. A workspace without the emoji shows ⏳ / ✓ / 🛎️. Upload steps are in docs/slack-emoji.md; new Slack apps get the `emoji:read` permission this needs. (#71)

Security (the guard)

- Jean's command can't be run under another name: a copy, a link, a variable, `$(which …)`, a PATH set on the line, or a program fed through `xargs`/`parallel`. Making a copy of it is stopped. (#69) - A lane can't change approval levels or Jean's config through Jean's own Python modules. (#70) - Code in a here-document is checked in the folder the line has moved into, and after `if`/`then`/`do`/`{` (before, it could go unread there). (#77)

Fixes

- No longer stopped by mistake: text in a here-document when the same line runs Jean's command by its full path (a PR comment, a review), harmless aliases (`alias ll='ls $HOME'`), a log named like Jean's (`test_guard.log`), a lane editing its own handoff notes with a here-document after `cd ~/.jean/lanes`. (#69, #72, #77) - Tell me posts and the evening digest survive a failed Slack post or a bridge restart. (#70)

item.title: Jean 0.4.6
item.description:
Jean 0.4.6

Changes since 0.4.5 (from d861961), merged into slack-tidy (6116176).

Slack bridge

- The bridge notices when its Slack connection dies and reconnects on its own (or restarts). `jean doctor` shows ✗ while it's down, and `jean watch` restarts a bridge that stays disconnected. (#59) - After a restart, `jean doctor` shows the bridge as starting instead of briefly ✗. If it keeps crashing at startup (a bad Slack token, say), doctor shows ✗ after 2 minutes instead of "starting" forever. (#62, #63) - `jean doctor` checks that Claude Code is 2.1.295 or later (needed for the guard to block when it can't run) and says to run `claude update` if not. (#61)

Security (the guard)

- A lane can start one exact Claude session, or have Jean restart one lane, once an owner approves that command (a new "session" approval). (#33, #53) - **Approvals asked for just before this update won't match after it** (command ids now keep spacing inside quotes): ask again. One time only. - Closes many ways a command could run something the guard didn't see: git remote helpers and settings that run programs, text piped or fed into a shell or an interpreter, `trap`, `watch`, `find -exec sh -c`, `$(…)` inside here-documents, AppleScript `do shell script`, awk `system()`, and variable tricks (array elements, `+=`, `printf -v`, export/declare). (#47, #50, #60) - Only an owner can turn overflow helpers on or change them, change the packages in Jean's own Python, or restart Jean's background services. Checking a service (`launchctl print`, `list`) is fine. (#54, #60) - A lane can write only its own handoff notes. The file-editing tools and shell commands follow the same rules, and a repository's own hooks need an owner's OK. (#41, #58) - More git holes closed: `git clone -c`/`--config` settings (any short form, bundled flags), `--git-dir`, `--separate-git-dir` by any short form, and a repo's `.git` put in place by mv/cp (any letter case, as macOS sees it). (#67)

Fixes

- The memory meter reads 1M-token context windows correctly. (#64) - No longer stopped by mistake: `claude --help` and other read-only claude subcommands (#65); a lane's own modules named like Jean's (`work.py`, `keys.py`, `connectors/`) (#66); `2>&1`, `git for-each-ref`, `git remote show`, `git rebase --exec 'make test'`, harmless sed edits, text in single quotes or in a quoted here-document (a PR body or release note naming a command), a PR title with an apostrophe, Jean's own Python run to look, a lane's own scripts and job temp folder. (#48, #50, #56, #60)

New

- Worker sessions (`jean spawn`): a lane with several independent tasks asks an owner once, naming the tasks; after the ✅ it starts one worker per task, each in its own git worktree and branch, closed when the approved hours are up. The ask lists each task's text, and workers get exactly that text and the reason you approved, even if the task changes later. A lane can ask for workers only for itself. Workers follow the lane's rules and still ask before merges and deploys. (#66, #68) - Settings › Connections: each tool has its own step-by-step setup page with live links (Setup steps button). (#55) - Overflow helpers: a busy lane can hand new tasks to a temporary second session (off until an owner turns it on). (#52, #57) - Updates: before an update rolls back, Jean checks the copy it would roll back to is complete and signed. (#49)

item.title: Jean 0.4.5
item.description:
Jean 0.4.5

Fixes

- Studio: in 0.4.4 every Studio message ended with no answer (Claude was started without the message). Fixed. A message typed before Studio has finished opening is now held and sent as soon as it is ready instead of being lost. The same bug stopped Settings › Keys from saving a key in 0.4.4; fixed too. (#30, #39) - Studio: a message typed early is never lost: if Studio can't open or no Claude is found, it goes back into the message box with a note. Pressing Stop just before a retry now always stops. (#40) - A specialist is never restarted to free up memory before it has written its handoff notes: Jean asks you to check on it instead. It is never started twice either. (#27) - Jean.app no longer crashes when a window closes while a command it started is being stopped. (#45) - `jean doctor` no longer tells a desktop Mac "Laptops don't have it" when it can't find the restart-after-power-failure setting. (#35)

Security

- The guard stops forged approvals and secret reads hidden behind wildcards, braces, variables, arrays, loops, `cd`, `xargs` and similar shell forms. (#38) - The guard stops writes into its own files through 17 tricky shell forms it used to miss. (#31) - The guard matches file names in any letter case, with accents, and through links, so CAPS or a shortcut can't sneak past it. (#37) - A read-only git command redirected into Jean's own files (for example, git log written over the approvals file) now counts as a write and is stopped. (#34) - False alarm fixed: commit messages and PR text that only mention Jean's own files are no longer blocked. Real writes to those files and secret reads are still stopped. (#32)

New

- Studio: a mic button types what you say into the message box (macOS asks for the microphone and speech recognition once), and Shift+Enter makes a new line while Enter still sends. (#36) - New setup guide page, "Your always-on Mac and restarts", and three new `jean doctor` checks: FileVault, automatic login, and restart after a power failure. (#29)

item.title: Jean 0.4.4
item.description:
Jean 0.4.4

  • Only you approve. A specialist can no longer act as you: code it writes for a tab stays a draft until you preview and publish it (hub › To approve), and an automation it changes turns off until you approve the new steps, which the Slack message now shows in full.
  • Jean.app proves itself to the hub without sending its key, and the hub's sign-in for your windows lives only in memory, so nothing on this Mac can copy it.
  • The Library never copies a file that points somewhere else, or anything from Jean's own folder.
  • Slack task cards say "Waiting on you" when a specialist needs your answer, and tick off every step when the task is done.
  • The phone hub setup accepts Cloudflare account tokens, and says plainly when a token is mistyped.

item.title: Jean 0.4.3
item.description:
Jean 0.4.3

  • **Updates install themselves.** From now on Jean checks every hour, installs updates and relaunches by itself.
  • **The hub on your phone (setup).** `jean tunnel setup` connects the hub to your own address behind Cloudflare sign-in, from one paste.
  • **Fewer false stops.** The guard no longer blocks read-only commands like awk, find and git branch --list, or notes that name a file. Real risks still need your check mark.
  • **Your plan, never an API key.** Lanes, relays and Studio never pick up an Anthropic API key from the Mac, so Jean always bills your Claude plan.
  • **Dev bench (off by default).** A nightly review of the lanes work, for Jeans developers.

item.title: Jean 0.4.2
item.description:
Jean 0.4.2

  • Slack works again: 0.4.1 stopped Jean from hearing messages, check marks and Approve/Deny buttons. Anything you sent in Slack since updating to 0.4.1, please send again.

item.title: Jean 0.4.1
item.description:
Jean 0.4.1

**Tidier Slack threads** - Send several messages in a row and Jean answers them together, once. - A "thanks" or "all good" gets a 👍 instead of a reply. - Each request ends as one message: the "On it" card turns into the answer. - Shorter answers, no repeated commands, and a new topic gets its own thread.

**Studio message queue** - Type while Studio is working: your message joins the task in progress. - If the task has just finished, it waits and runs next. Stop hands it back.
